requirement: Account for implementation aspects (side-channel resistance, secure implementation) when procuring or deploying cryptographic modules; require side-channel-hardened implementations per the guideline.
evidence_quote: Updates in the areas of side-channel analysis, QKD and seed generation for random number generators.
evidence_location: Version history (2023-01 entry); Section 1.4 Implementation Aspects

requirement: Consider crypto-agility features during the benefit/risk analysis of future products or systems.
evidence_quote: ANSSI emphasises that crypto-agility features must be considered during the benefit/risk analysis of future products or systems, as it provides a way to include these new components.

requirement: Conduct a threat analysis and evaluation of the worst-case implementation before implementing crypto-agility.
evidence_quote: A threat analysis and evaluation of the worst-case implementation must be conducted beforehand.

requirement: Implement algorithmic crypto-agility wherever the context allows; otherwise use the highest-security parameter set, and consider parameterisation agility only if efficiency prevents that.
evidence_quote: Algorithmic crypto-agility should be implemented whenever the context allows it. If not, it is recommended to use the parameter set with the highest security of a cryptographic algorithm, when such a parameter set exists.

requirement: Implement crypto-agility consistently across all sub-systems so that components (e.g. protocols, signature handling) can adapt to new algorithm outputs and sizes.
evidence_quote: Crypto-agility should be implemented in a consistent manner across all sub-systems of the system.

requirement: Implement crypto-agility without breaking system functionality; handle old and new keys during transitions and size the system for the worst-case cryptographic volume and timing.
evidence_quote: If crypto-agility is applied via a configuration file or a negotiation phase, the system must be able to work under any result of the negotiation phase, which means dimensioning it to the worst case scenario, in terms of cryptographic volume and timing performances.

requirement: Protect integrity and authenticity of updates with the highest-confidence cryptographic mechanisms; do not share update keys across devices and protect the update key with a hardware security element.
evidence_quote: The integrity and authenticity protection of updates must be assured by cryptographic mechanisms in which confidence is at its highest.

requirement: Do not use the same update keys across multiple devices, and protect the update key using a hardware security element.
evidence_quote: Update keys should not be common to multiple devices. Whatever the cryptographic means implemented, a hardware security element should be used to ensure the protection of the update key.

requirement: Implement protection against replay of outdated updates for software updates.
evidence_quote: Protection against replay attacks (which consist in sending an outdated update) must be implemented in the case of software updates.

requirement: Ensure algorithm selection/negotiation cannot result in an undesired algorithm; do not allow deprecated algorithms in new systems; restrict security downgrade, with cipher-suite blacklists or minimal configuration such as TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV.
evidence_quote: deprecated cryptographic algorithms must not be allowed for new systems. Black lists of cipher suites, or at least some kind of minimal configuration (as TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV for example), should be implemented.

requirement: Protect cryptographic configuration with authentication (or at least integrity) methods and anti-replay means.
evidence_quote: The configuration must be protected with authentication (or at least integrity) methods and anti-replay means.

requirement: For static (non-updatable) implementations, implement from the outset all algorithms the product may need and use configuration to select the desired subset.
evidence_quote: all the algorithms that shall be used in the product must be implemented from the get-go and crypto-agility is a means to ensure the use of the desired (subset of) algorithm(s).
